name: Soul Glo
label: Epitaph
lede: A Philadelphia band built so the people who didn't fit the city's punk shows had somewhere to stand, now with a Pitchfork 8.5, a Coachella slot and a bass section that changes by the year.

eras.title: Outsiders in every room
eras.text: Pierce Jordan and Ruben Polo start a band in Philadelphia for kids who fit neither the city's hardcore shows nor its punk ones. Two untitled records, a rotating rhythm section and a Missouri highway stop later, the lineup that would make the big records is in place.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The Ringer · Loud Fast Philly · Wikipedia: Soul Glo
years.h: Pierce Jordan and Ruben Polo start Soul Glo in Philadelphia
years.p: The first lineup is a quartet: [[Pierce Jordan|6a8a8824-41e0-422e-a17e-b9b0517d89f2]] on vocals, Ruben Polo on guitar, Ethan Brennan on bass and Jamie Sokol on drums.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone describes the founding idea as playing local shows in Philadelphia alongside bands that had no place in the city's punk or hardcore bills. The Ringer reports that Jordan grew up in Calvert County, Maryland, in the suburbs of Washington, D.C., and moved to Philadelphia in the early 2010s.

Loud Fast Philly, the local DIY interview series, has a conversation with Jordan and Polo about coming up as outsiders in both Black communities and mostly white punk spaces.

years.p: A second record with no title, jazzier guitar chords and a William Blake poem in the mix, out on SRA Records.
years.xp: Rolling Stone points to the literary reference, Blake's "The Little Black Boy", as a sign the band was already wider than its hardcore label.

years.h: Out of town with Old Gray, including Brooklyn and Boston
years.p: Soul Glo support Old Gray on a short Northeast weekend run, among their first shows beyond Philadelphia.

years.h: GG Guerra joins on bass and samples
years.p: Multi-instrumentalist Gianmarco "GG" Guerra arrives, the producer and programmer the band's sound will later lean on.

years.h: TJ Stevenson replaces Jamie Sokol on drums
years.p: [[Pierce Jordan|6a8a8824-41e0-422e-a17e-b9b0517d89f2]], Polo, Guerra and Stevenson are now the lineup that will make the next three records.

years.big: Held together by dried tears and blood
years.h: GG Guerra is arrested on the way to St. Louis
years.p: Missouri State Highway Patrol arrested Guerra en route to a St. Louis show; the band's own summary of those years is the line above, quoted by The Ringer.
years.xp: The band raised $15,000 for Guerra's bail. The Ringer quotes a band statement listing "constant van issues, mental issues, shit w the law" as the price of touring.

eras.title: Everything in one record
eras.text: The 2019 LP is where the band stops sounding like a screamo revival and starts pulling in hip-hop, noise and jazz fusion. A pandemic-year EP keeps the pace.

years.cap: The Nigga in Me Is Me, SRA Records
years.src: The Ringer · Rolling Stone · Wikipedia: Soul Glo
years.h: The Nigga in Me Is Me drags hardcore into the present
years.p: On SRA Records, the LP pulls in hip-hop, noise and jazz fusion, and Jordan's confrontational titles become the band's calling card.
years.xp: Jordan has said the original idea was a hardcore band that could use a word most hardcore audiences avoid, and make a room uncomfortable enough to keep listening. The single from the record, "Too Late, Nigger I'm Tired", shows the method.

years.h: Songs to Yeet at the Sun EP on Secret Voice
years.p: With the singles "(Quietly) Do the Right Thing" and "29", it's the last release before the Epitaph deal.

eras.title: The Epitaph deal
eras.text: A Philadelphia band that was still raising bail money three years earlier signs to a major punk label and goes out on the road as the headline of its own story.

years.h: Soul Glo sign to Epitaph and put out two DisNigga EPs
years.p: DisNigga, Vol. 1 and DisNigga, Vol. 2 are their first releases for Epitaph.

eras.title: Diaspora Problems
eras.text: The record that puts Soul Glo on year-end lists arrives in the same months the band loses its guitarist and rebuilds around a new bass section.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The Ringer · Wikipedia: Soul Glo
years.h: Ruben Polo leaves; Rob Blackwell and Leon Da Boss join
years.p: Polo, a founding guitarist, departs after an ex-boyfriend accused him of rape by deception, according to Rolling Stone; Polo denies it.
years.xp: The Ringer noted Polo's exit, along with a cancelled Circa Survive opening slot, in the weeks before release. Guerra moved from bass to guitar and programming, and Rob Blackwell and Leon Da Boss came in on bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: Diaspora Problems · Album of the Year · Bandcamp Daily · The Ringer · Brooklyn Vegan
years.p: Pitchfork gave the Epitaph debut 8.5 and ranked it No. 36 on its best albums of 2022; Metacritic scores it 86.
years.xp:
The Ringer says it was recorded in December 2020 to August 2021, produced by Guerra and Evan Bernard with Will Yip on mix and master, and Wikipedia gives the release as March 25, 2022. The title comes from a Facebook event, where a promoter's blurb for Soul Glo read only "Philadelphia, diaspora problems", Jordan told Bandcamp Daily.

Guests are people Jordan already knew, with the exception of Mother Maryrose (Jordan to Bandcamp Daily): McKinley Dixon and Lojii, Kathryn Edwards of Thirdface, Philly rapper Zula Wildheart and BEARCAT. Elsewhere Vulture had it at No. 5, The Wire at No. 12 and NPR at No. 49; Rolling Stone later put it in its 100 Greatest Punk Albums.

years.h: Lead single "Jump!! (Or Get Jumped!!!((by the future)))" lands
years.p: The video is the first real look at the new record's combination of breakneck hardcore and hip-hop.

years.h: The Half-a-USA tour with Show Me the Body and Wifigawd
years.p: A cross-country run pairing Show Me the Body and Wifigawd with Soul Glo.

years.h: My Chemical Romance take Soul Glo and Turnstile to an arena
years.p: Soul Glo open the My Chemical Romance reunion show at PNC Arena in North Carolina alongside [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]].

yt: Live at Mohawk Place, Buffalo, Nov 14, 2022
years.h: A Northeast run with City of Caterpillar and Thirdface
years.p: Soul Glo co-headline with the screamo band City of Caterpillar and Philadelphia's Thirdface, closing the loop on the band's earliest influences.

eras.title: Coachella and the next record
eras.text: The band plays a big festival stage, settles on a new bass player and announces a follow-up with Mannequin Pussy on it.

years.h: Soul Glo play the 22nd Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival
years.p: A Philadelphia hardcore band walks out at Coachella, one of the biggest American festivals.
years.xp: Rolling Stone says Jordan performed in a thong, as he had jokingly promised years earlier. Rolling Stone dates the Coachella set 2024; Wikipedia gives 2023.

years.p: Wikipedia lists Hightower as the third person in the bass slot since 2022, alongside Blackwell and Da Boss.

years.h: Na I'm Gon Grab Allat is announced for January 15, 2027
years.p: The Epitaph album's lead single "February Theory" features [[Mannequin Pussy|e160f589-dbe6-4b8f-88b5-f528ff4443b4]], and Jordan says it's about his failures in relationships with men.
years.xp: Kerrang lists guests including Bear Regisford of Mannequin Pussy, Tati Salazar of Commitment, Tunde Adebimpe, MIKE, BbyNutha and Eugene Robinson.
